application_context.summary:
Application domain: Corporate fleet management.

This is a local FastAPI application that manages persistent domain resources through REST endpoints.

domain_invariants.requirement: Vehicle and maintenance ids are positive immutable integers; non-positive ids are treated as not found.

A maintenance references exactly one existing vehicle, has type PREVENTIVE, CORRECTIVE, INSPECTION, or REPAIR, title length 3..120, optional description length 0..2000, and planned_end strictly later than planned_start.
Maintenance status transitions are SCHEDULED to IN_PROGRESS or CANCELLED, and IN_PROGRESS to COMPLETED or CANCELLED; COMPLETED and CANCELLED are terminal.
Active maintenance intervals for a vehicle, namely SCHEDULED or IN_PROGRESS records, must not overlap; touching endpoints do not overlap.
Starting maintenance requires the vehicle current state MAINTENANCE. Completing or cancelling the last active maintenance atomically moves the vehicle to AVAILABLE or OUT_OF_SERVICE.
Maintenance cancellation is historical and immutable: a cancelled record keeps its planned schedule, cancellation timestamp, and reason of 3..500 characters and is never deleted.

Every maintenance status change appends an immutable history event containing previous_status, new_status, effective_at in UTC, actor id, and optional reason; history events are never modified or removed independently.
A user may create, read, amend, start, complete, or cancel only maintenance requested by that user; admins may operate all maintenance. Vehicle management is admin-only.
A maintenance record with history cannot be deleted. A vehicle with any maintenance cannot be deleted, preserving planning and cancellation history.
All maintenance timestamps are UTC ISO-8601 with second precision; actual_end must not precede actual_start, and cancellation timestamp must not precede planned_start.

List order is ascending immutable id, using limit 1..100 default 20 and after_id > 0; results return items and next_after_id, null when exhausted.
New maintenance is SCHEDULED and creates a SCHEDULED history event at creation time.

Maintenance status transitions are SCHEDULED to IN_PROGRESS or CANCELLED, and IN_PROGRESS to COMPLETED or CANCELLED; COMPLETED and CANCELLED are terminal.
Active maintenance intervals for a vehicle, namely SCHEDULED or IN_PROGRESS records, must not overlap; touching endpoints do not overlap.
Starting maintenance requires the vehicle current state MAINTENANCE. Completing or cancelling the last active maintenance atomically moves the vehicle to AVAILABLE or OUT_OF_SERVICE.
Maintenance cancellation is historical and immutable: a cancelled record keeps its planned schedule, cancellation timestamp, and reason of 3..500 characters and is never deleted.

Every maintenance status change appends an immutable history event containing previous_status, new_status, effective_at in UTC, actor id, and optional reason; history events are never modified or removed independently.
A user may create, read, amend, start, complete, or cancel only maintenance requested by that user; admins may operate all maintenance. Vehicle management is admin-only.
A maintenance record with history cannot be deleted. A vehicle with any maintenance cannot be deleted, preserving planning and cancellation history.
All maintenance timestamps are UTC ISO-8601 with second precision; actual_end must not precede actual_start, and cancellation timestamp must not precede planned_start.

application_context.summary:
Application domain: Corporate fleet management.
Backend variant: Maintenance planning, cancellation, and history.
This is a local FastAPI application that manages persistent domain resources through REST endpoints.
Apply the shared authorization, validation, controlled-error, and transaction conventions specified for the endpoint.

domain_invariants.requirement: Vehicle and maintenance ids are positive immutable integers; non-positive ids are treated as not found.

A maintenance references exactly one existing vehicle, has type PREVENTIVE, CORRECTIVE, INSPECTION, or REPAIR, title length 3..120, optional description length 0..2000, and planned_end strictly later than planned_start.
Maintenance status transitions are SCHEDULED to IN_PROGRESS or CANCELLED, and IN_PROGRESS to COMPLETED or CANCELLED; COMPLETED and CANCELLED are terminal.
Active maintenance intervals for a vehicle, namely SCHEDULED or IN_PROGRESS records, must not overlap; touching endpoints do not overlap.
Starting maintenance requires the vehicle current state MAINTENANCE. Completing or cancelling the last active maintenance atomically moves the vehicle to AVAILABLE or OUT_OF_SERVICE.
Maintenance cancellation is historical and immutable: a cancelled record keeps its planned schedule, cancellation timestamp, and reason of 3..500 characters and is never deleted.

Every maintenance status change appends an immutable history event containing previous_status, new_status, effective_at in UTC, actor id, and optional reason; history events are never modified or removed independently.
A user may create, read, amend, start, complete, or cancel only maintenance requested by that user; admins may operate all maintenance. Vehicle management is admin-only.
A maintenance record with history cannot be deleted. A vehicle with any maintenance cannot be deleted, preserving planning and cancellation history.
All maintenance timestamps are UTC ISO-8601 with second precision; actual_end must not precede actual_start, and cancellation timestamp must not precede planned_start.

seed_and_operational_context: Roles are user and admin. Private endpoints deny by default and require a valid non-expired server-side Bearer session token.
List order is ascending immutable id, using limit 1..100 default 20 and after_id > 0; results return items and next_after_id, null when exhausted.
New maintenance is SCHEDULED and creates a SCHEDULED history event at creation time.

endpoint_contract.formal_requirement: The system shall expose POST /maintenances/{maintenance_id}/start as an authenticated endpoint accepting a positive id and JSON actual_start; it shall permit requester or admin to start only SCHEDULED maintenance at or after planned_start when the vehicle is MAINTENANCE, atomically create an IN_PROGRESS history event and update status, be non-idempotent, and emit only 200, 400, 401, 403, 404, 409, 415, 422, 429, 500, or 503.

error_responses.error_model: controlled AppException / existing backend error handling
